The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
-1\,250,\,-1\,235,\,-1\,220,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=15:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =15 \\  & =-1\,235-(-1\,250) \\  & =-1\,220-(-1\,235) \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-1\,250\,+(n-1)\cdot 15 \\  & =-1\,250+15n-15 \\  & =15n-1\,265.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={15n-1\,265:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}15N-1\,265 & =19\,300 \\ 15N & =20\,565 \\ N & =\frac{20\,565}{15} \\ N & =1\,371\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={15n-1\,265:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 1\,371}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $1\,371$ elements, we must have $|A|=1\,371.$
